# 🫥 NoMount Suite Loads root modules without mounting anything, RRO overlays included. No `overlayfs`, no `tmpfs`: the **Prism** kernel engine redirects VFS lookups, so nothing shows up in `/proc/mounts`. It is a metamodule. > **Beta.** Reports from other phones, managers and odd modules move it to > stable. `nomount export` builds the bundle, hide list redacted.
Status Hiding Rules Checks Duck Detector
## Install Each [release](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/NoMount-Suite/releases/latest) has two zips: | Zip | For | | :--- | :--- | | `00_NoMount-Module` | A kernel with the engine built in: the [`BakaSu`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-BakaSu_NMS/releases), [`KsuNext`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-KsuNext_NMS/releases) or [`SukiSu`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-SukiSu_NMS/releases) OnePlus kernels, or your own build with `CONFIG_NOMOUNT=y` from [`hookless/`](hookless/) | | `01_NoMount-Module-LKM` | A stock GKI kernel. It loads the engine as a module at boot (android12-5.10 to android17-6.18) | Flash it from your manager, reboot, then check from a root shell: ```sh alias nomount=/data/adb/modules/meta-nomount/bin/arm64-v8a/nomount nomount check # want: verdict: clean, 0 failed, 0 unmeasured ``` Needs arm64 and KernelSU (or a fork) or Magisk. SUSFS is not needed. Updates are the same flash and keep your settings. Magisk has no WebUI, so on Magisk use the commands below from a root shell. ## Safe Guard boot Let it boot twice more: after three failed boots the Suite parks itself. To park it by hand from recovery: ```sh mkdir -p /data/adb/nomount && touch /data/adb/nomount/disabled ``` ### If it parked itself Nothing is injected until you re-arm it. `/data/adb/nomount/incident.log` says why it parked; copy it first (WebUI: **Checks → Copy incident**). Then re-arm in **Checks → Bootloop guard**, or from a root shell, and reboot: ```sh rm /data/adb/nomount/disabled /data/adb/nomount/bootcount ``` ## Commands The WebUI does all of this. From a shell: `nomount check`, `reload`, `uid block `, `whiteout add `, `export`. `nomount --help` has the rest. To report a problem, paste what **Checks → Copy report** copies; if we need more, **Checks → Developer tools → Export** writes a zip to attach. To hide one rule from named apps, rather than from everyone: ```sh nomount vfs add --uid-excluded com.google.android.gms /rom/path /data/adb/... ``` Entries are package names, globs or appids, comma separated. An appid covers that app under every user, work profile included. To hide an **absorbed APK** the same way, list those apps in `/data/adb/nomount/apkscope`, one per line — absent means off, which is the default. A rule added this way lasts until the next reboot: nothing writes it to disk. For content that must come back every boot, ship it in a module. ## Building ```sh cargo test && ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk scripts/package.sh --build --lite ``` That builds the 00_ zip, for a kernel with NoMount built in. Without `--lite`, `package.sh` also packages the 01_ zip and stops unless the eight `module/lkm/nomount-*.ko` from CI's `build.yaml` are there; a release build (`--version vX.Y.Z`) also needs `module/bin/ko-loader-arm64`. ## License and credits GPL-3.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). A rewrite of **[maxsteeel/nomount](https://github.com/maxsteeel/nomount)**. Thanks to [HymoFS](https://github.com/Anatdx/HymoFS), [A7mdwassa](https://github.com/A7mdwassa), [ZQZCC](https://github.com/ZQZCC), [backslashxx](https://github.com/backslashxx), [KernelSU](https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU), SukiSU-Ultra, [SUSFS](https://gitlab.com/simonpunk/susfs4ksu) and every tester. Modifying a kernel can brick a phone or lose data. Use at your own risk.

🫥 NoMount Suite

Loads root modules without mounting anything, RRO overlays included. No

overlayfs, no tmpfs: the Prism kernel engine redirects VFS lookups, so

nothing shows up in /proc/mounts. It is a metamodule.

> Beta. Reports from other phones, managers and odd modules move it to

> stable. nomount export builds the bundle, hide list redacted.

Status Hiding Rules Checks Duck Detector

Install

Each release has two zips:

| Zip | For |

| :--- | :--- |

| 00_NoMount-Module | A kernel with the engine built in: the BakaSu, KsuNext or SukiSu OnePlus kernels, or your own build with CONFIG_NOMOUNT=y from hookless/ |

| 01_NoMount-Module-LKM | A stock GKI kernel. It loads the engine as a module at boot (android12-5.10 to android17-6.18) |

Flash it from your manager, reboot, then check from a root shell:

alias nomount=/data/adb/modules/meta-nomount/bin/arm64-v8a/nomount
nomount check      # want: verdict: clean, 0 failed, 0 unmeasured

Needs arm64 and KernelSU (or a fork) or Magisk. SUSFS is not needed. Updates

are the same flash and keep your settings. Magisk has no WebUI, so on Magisk use

the commands below from a root shell.

Safe Guard boot

Let it boot twice more: after three failed boots the Suite parks itself. To

park it by hand from recovery:

mkdir -p /data/adb/nomount && touch /data/adb/nomount/disabled

If it parked itself

Nothing is injected until you re-arm it. /data/adb/nomount/incident.log says

why it parked; copy it first (WebUI: Checks → Copy incident). Then re-arm in

Checks → Bootloop guard, or from a root shell, and reboot:

rm /data/adb/nomount/disabled /data/adb/nomount/bootcount

Commands

The WebUI does all of this. From a shell: nomount check, reload,

uid block , whiteout add , export. nomount --help has the

rest. To report a problem, paste what Checks → Copy report copies; if we

need more, Checks → Developer tools → Export writes a zip to attach.

To hide one rule from named apps, rather than from everyone:

nomount vfs add --uid-excluded com.google.android.gms /rom/path /data/adb/...

Entries are package names, globs or appids, comma separated. An appid covers that

app under every user, work profile included. To hide an absorbed APK the same

way, list those apps in /data/adb/nomount/apkscope, one per line — absent means

off, which is the default.

A rule added this way lasts until the next reboot: nothing writes it to disk. For

content that must come back every boot, ship it in a module.

Building

cargo test && ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk scripts/package.sh --build --lite

That builds the 00_ zip, for a kernel with NoMount built in. Without --lite,

package.sh also packages the 01_ zip and stops unless the eight

module/lkm/nomount-*.ko from CI's build.yaml are there; a release build

(--version vX.Y.Z) also needs module/bin/ko-loader-arm64.

License and credits

GPL-3.0, see LICENSE. A rewrite of

maxsteeel/nomount. Thanks to

HymoFS, A7mdwassa,

ZQZCC, backslashxx,

KernelSU, SukiSU-Ultra,

SUSFS and every tester.

Modifying a kernel can brick a phone or lose data. Use at your own risk.
